description: MAINTAINER RULING #984, Q2: coalescing is REQUIRED, not permitted -- `If a prior invocation is still running when the next interval arrives, the implementation MUST queue that occurrence and run it once the handler is free` (spec/interaction-events.md:189-196). The blocker is a once-firing `on_key` rather than the `every` body itself, deliberately: a handler that blocks in its OWN body re-queues during every drained invocation, so it degrades to running back to back and the program only ends at `ol-limit` -- correct behaviour, but useless as a fixture. Here the `every 4` body is instantaneous and a single key press at tick 4 holds the execution thread for nine ticks. Measured: the key and the tick-4 interval are claimed into the SAME batch (spec/interaction-events.md:84-89 orders `on_key` before due `every`), so the `every` handler sits claimed while the `on_key` body's `wait 9` runs ticks 5-13; its intervals arrive on schedule at ticks 8 and 12 and are queued. When `on_key` returns, the claimed invocation runs (first `print`) and the queued one is drained immediately after it (second `print`). The critical detail is that the outer `wait 4` has ALREADY spent its last tick -- the whole episode happens inside the tick-4 dispatch -- so there is no later checkpoint. A runtime that defers the drain to the next event-loop checkpoint prints ONCE here and silently loses the occurrence, which is indistinguishable from the `drop it` reading the ruling rejects; that was a real defect in the first implementation of this issue, caught by review rather than by any fixture. Measured against mutated runtimes: dropping the missed occurrence prints 1, deferring the drain prints 1, and a fixed-delay clock prints 1. An UNCAPPED queue prints 2 here and is NOT detected by this fixture. Two occurrences are in fact missed (the intervals at ticks 8 and 12) and they coalesce into the one slot, but the main line ends immediately after the drain, so ruling #984 closes the run and discards the backlog before an uncapped queue could show itself. That reading is pinned by `every-queue-coalesces-to-one` instead, which keeps the run open past the blockage.
